gap: No result ChatGPT got states that EVDANCE's own US store sells the native NEMA 14-30 24 A charger for $229.95 in both the J1772 and NACS versions on 2026-11-17, which is $40 and $50 below the $269.99 and $279.99 Amazon prices that Plug & Range and The Charge Curve quote. None of them says either that J+ Booster's store, where the Booster 2 costs $749, sells no 14-30 adapter at all.
standout_why: I compared against plugandrange.com/portable-chargers/nema-14-30 (updated 2026-09-15, prices dated 2026-11-16) and thechargecurve.com/home-ev-chargers/best-nema-14-30 (updated 2026-10-17, prices dated 2026-11-16). Both rank the same field: EVDANCE 14-30 J1772 at $269.99, EVDANCE 14-30 NACS at $279.99, Grizzl-E Mini at $349.99, SEGUMA at $251.99 and $269.99, and Splitvolt unpriced or excluded. All of their prices come from Amazon. Neither gives a maker-store price. Neither says that the NACS and J1772 versions cost the same at the maker. Neither covers J+ Booster 2, which ChatGPT searched for, or whether it can use a 14-30 outlet at all.
decides: This backs EVDANCE's native 14-30 unit as the best-value pick and lowers its price by $40–50 against every rival page. For Tesla drivers, it makes the EVDANCE 14-30 NACS ($229.95, native plug, no adapter) cheaper than ChatGPT's 'Best for Tesla' pick, a $300 Tesla Mobile Connector plus an adapter sold separately. I could not open a Tesla price page to confirm the Tesla total. Our current page has no 14-30 NACS row and should add one. The finding rules out J+ Booster 2 for this question: it costs $749 and its maker sells no 14-30 adapter. It also rules out Grizzl-E Mini at $349.99, which costs more than EVDANCE, is out of stock at the maker, and charges no faster on a 30 A circuit.
